'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Gaza war]]
**[[Gaza war hostage crisis]]
***[[Hamas]] releases a video showing a speech by two [[Israelis|Israeli]] [[hostage]]s in [[Gaza Strip|Gaza]] kidnapped during the [[Nova music festival massacre]] in 2023. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/hamas-releases-video-israeli-hostages-held-gaza-2025-09-05/ (Reuters)] [https://www.jpost.com/israel-news/defense-news/article-866456 (''The Jerusalem Post'')]
*[[Kivu conflict]]
**[[M23 campaign (2022–present)|M23 campaign]]
***The [[United Nations Human Rights Office]] reports that [[March 23 Movement|M23 rebel]]s, the [[Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo|Congolese armed forces]], and other groups in eastern [[Democratic Republic of the Congo]] have committed serious abuses, including killings, torture, [[sexual violence]], and [[Children in the military|child recruitment]], some of which may constitute [[war crime]]s and [[crimes against humanity]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/m23-congolese-forces-may-have-committed-war-crimes-congo-un-rights-report-finds-2025-09-05/ (Reuters)]
*[[War on drugs]], [[United States–Venezuela relations]]
**The [[Second presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] deploys ten [[Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II|F-35]] fighter jets to [[Puerto Rico]] to take part in [[military action]] against [[drug cartel]]s in [[Venezuela]] and [[Latin America]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/sep/05/trump-fighter-planes-puerto-rico-venezuela-drug-cartel (''The Guardian'')]
**[[Bolivarian Military Aviation of Venezuela|Venezuelan Air Force]] [[General Dynamics F-16 Fighting Falcon|F-16]] fighter jets fly over the [[USS Jason Dunham|USS ''Jason Dunham'']] in [[international waters]] for a second time in 24 hours as tensions mount between the [[United States]] and [[Venezuela]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/venezuela-flies-military-aircraft-over-u-s-navy-ship-for-second-time-uss-jason-dunham/ (CBS News)] 
**[[President of Venezuela|Venezuelan president]] [[Nicolás Maduro]] accuses the U.S. of seeking a [[regime change]] in [[Venezuela]] under the guise of combating cartels. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/trump-plays-down-possible-regime-change-venezuela-us-deploys-stealth-fighter-2025-09-05/ (Reuters)]
**[[Caribbean Airlines]] halts all flights between [[Trinidad and Tobago]] and Venezuela for the entire month of September due to the military situation in the region. [https://guyanatimesgy.com/caribbean-airlines-halts-all-tt-venezuela-flights-with-immediate-effect/ (''Guyana Times'')]
*[[Anglophone Crisis]]
**A [[Improvised explosive device|roadside bomb]] kills seven [[Cameroon]]ian [[Cameroon Armed Forces|soldiers]] in the [[Southwest Region (Cameroon)|Southwest Region]]. An [[English language|English-speaking]] separatist group claims responsibility for the bombing. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/cameroon-separatists-claim-deadly-roadside-attack-killed-7-125318634 (ABC News)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**At least 63 people are killed, including seven [[Nigerian Army|soldiers]], and others are reported missing in attacks by [[Boko Haram]] [[Jihadism|jihadists]] in Darul Jamal, [[Borno State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/boko-haram-kills-dozens-house-house-attack-nigerias-northeast-residents-say-2025-09-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Kidnapping in Nigeria]]
**Eight security officials are killed, four others are seriously injured, and five [[Chinese people|Chinese]] workers are kidnapped, with four rescued afterwards, in an attack on a [[Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps]] convoy in [[Edo State]], Nigeria. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/gunmen-nigeria-attack-chinese-workers-kill-security-officials-2025-09-06/ (Reuters)]
*[[Terrorism in India]]
**Lashkar-e-Jihadi warns police that multiple terrorist attacks involving 34 explosive-laden vehicles and 14 terrorists are being planned for the [[Ganesh Chaturthi]] finale on Saturday in [[Mumbai]], [[Maharashtra]], [[India]], causing security to be tightened. [https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/34-human-bombs-planted-in-vehicles-mumbai-police-receive-terror-threat-on-whatsapp-lashkar-e-jihadi-message-cites-14-pakistani-terrorists-14kg-rdx/articleshow/123713402.cms (''The Times of India'')]

'''Disasters and accidents''' 
*A bus carrying tourists plunges down a hill in [[Uva Province]], [[Sri Lanka]], killing at least 15 people and injuring 15 others. [https://indianexpress.com/article/world/sri-lanka-bus-crash-deaths-10231848/ (''Indian Express'')]
*Eleven people are reported missing, including children and an infant, and three others are rescued when a [[hippopotamus]] capsizes a boat on the [[Sassandra River]] near [[Buyo, Ivory Coast|Buyo]] in [[Ivory Coast]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/hippo-capsizes-boat-ivory-coast-children-baby-missing/ (CBS News)]
*A man is killed in a [[shark attack]] off [[Long Reef (New South Wales)|Long Reef beach]] in [[New South Wales]], [[Australia]]. The species of [[shark]] is currently unknown but it is believed to be a large shark due to the injuries recorded. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2025/sep/06/fatal-shark-attack-long-reef-beach-sydney-northern-beaches-nsw (''The Guardian'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[2023–2025 mpox epidemic]]
**[[World Health Organization]] [[Director-General of the World Health Organization|director-general]] [[Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus]] declares that [[mpox]] is no longer a [[public health emergency of international concern]], citing a consistent decline in cases in [[Africa]]. [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/mpox-no-longer-an-emergency-concerns-remain-health-body-says-2025-09-05/ (Reuters)]
*[[Portugal]] records [[List of extreme temperatures in Portugal|its hottest and driest summer]] since measurements began in 1931, with an average maximum temperature of {{convert|30.78|C|F}} and only 24% of normal rainfall, conditions that contributed to [[2025 European and Mediterranean wildfires#Portugal|recent wildfires]]. [https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/portugal-records-hottest-driest-summer-since-1931-weather-agency-9224888 (AFP via NDTV)]

'''International relations'''
*[[China–Pakistan relations]], [[China–Pakistan Economic Corridor]]
**During a [[state visit]] to [[Beijing]], [[Pakistan]]i [[Prime Minister of Pakistan|prime minister]] [[Shehbaz Sharif]] announces new US$8.5 billion investment agreements with [[China]], including $7 billion in a [[memorandum of understanding]] and $1.5 billion in joint ventures between the two countries. [https://apnews.com/article/pakistan-china-investment-agreement-beijing-70ca7b7098c11acf9a9d520328476c68 (AP)]
*[[Finland–Latvia relations]], [[Belarus–European Union border crisis]]
**[[Finland]] accepts [[Latvia]]'s request to deploy [[Finnish Border Guard|border guards]] at the [[Belarus–Latvia border]] to help manage increased [[Belarusian diaspora|migration from Belarus]], with [[Estonia]] and [[Lithuania]] also providing support. [https://www.reuters.com/world/finnish-border-guards-aid-latvia-amid-migrant-inflow-belarus-2025-09-05/ (Reuters)]
*[[Finland–Palestine relations]], [[Diplomatic impact of the Gaza war]]
**[[Finland]] joins the [[July 2025 Conference on the Implementation of the Two-State Solution#New York Declaration|New York Declaration]] calling for the end of the [[Gaza war]] and advancing a [[two-state solution]] to the [[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/finland-joins-declaration-two-state-solution-between-israel-palestinians-2025-09-05/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*The [[European Commission]] fines [[Google Inc.|Google]] {{Euro}}2.95 billion (US$3.47 billion) for allegedly abusing its position as the leading [[search engine]] to commit [[competition law|anti-trust violation]]s in the [[online advertising|advertising technology]] space. [https://www.dw.com/en/european-commission-fines-google-in-ad-tech-antitrust-case/a-73899986 (DW)]
*A [[Sweden|Swedish]] [[District courts of Sweden|district court]] acquits former [[National Security Council (Sweden)|national security adviser]] [[Henrik Landerholm]] of severe [[negligence]] after he left classified documents in an unlocked hotel [[safe]], ruling that his actions did not meet the threshold required for conviction. [https://www.reuters.com/world/swedish-ex-national-security-adviser-cleared-negligence-case-2025-09-05/ (Reuters)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2025 British cabinet reshuffle]]
**[[Angela Rayner]] resigns as [[Deputy Prime Minister of the United Kingdom]] and leaves her other government posts amid a [[scandal]] over a tax underpayment on a property she owns in [[Hove]], [[East Sussex]].  [https://news.sky.com/story/angela-rayner-to-resign-from-government-after-admitting-to-not-paying-enough-stamp-duty-sky-news-understands-duty-13424204 (Sky News)]
**[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Keir Starmer]] conducts a [[cabinet reshuffle]] and appoints [[Foreign Secretary (United Kingdom)|foreign secretary]] [[David Lammy]] as the new deputy PM and [[Secretary of State for Justice]] [[Shabana Mahmood]] as the new [[home secretary]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/live/c0lk8ye1979t (BBC News)]
*[[2025 Georgian local elections]]
**[[Georgia (country)|Georgian]] [[President of Georgia|president]] [[Mikheil Kavelashvili]] [[pardon]]s opposition politicians [[Mamuka Khazaradze]] and Badri Japaridze, allowing them to run in the upcoming elections after serving prison sentences for refusing to testify before [[Parliament of Georgia|parliament]]. [http://reuters.com/world/georgian-president-pardons-two-opposition-politicians-ahead-municipal-elections-2025-09-05/ (Reuters)]
*[[2025 Samoan general election]]
**Official results show that the [[Faʻatuatua i le Atua Samoa ua Tasi|FAST]] party led by [[Laʻauli Leuatea Schmidt]] wins the election by a [[Landslide victory|landslide]], securing 30 out of the 50 [[Legislative Assembly of Samoa|Legislative Assembly]] seats. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/5/fast-to-retain-power-after-samoan-election-victory-confirmed (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/samoa-general-election-final-vote-count-completed-official-results-due-tonight/4UFSJ7LK2BFABCFAQI4CKZQJ6M/ (''The New Zealand Herald'')]
*[[2025 Thai political crisis]]
**The [[House of Representatives (Thailand)|House of Representatives]] of [[Thailand]] elects [[Anutin Charnvirakul]], leader of the conservative opposition [[Bhumjaithai Party]], as [[Prime Minister of Thailand|the country's prime minister]], replacing [[Paetongtarn Shinawatra]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/9/5/thai-parliament-elects-anutin-charnvirakul-as-prime-minister-2 (Al Jazeera)]
*[[List of executive orders in the second Trump presidency|Executive orders in the second Trump presidency]]
**[[President of the United States|U.S. president]] [[Donald Trump]] signs an [[executive order]] unofficially renaming the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] to the Department of War. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cgr9r4qr0ppo (BBC News)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[AI boom]]
**[[European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking]]
***The [[Jupiter Booster|Jupiter]] [[supercomputer]], capable of at least one quintillion calculations per second with 24,000 [[Nvidia]] chips, is inaugurated in [[Jülich]], [[North Rhine-Westphalia]], [[Germany]], marking Europe's first system considered internationally competitive in [[Machine learning|training]] [[artificial intelligence]] models. On a partial system test, Jupiter has achieved a preliminary 793.4 Petaflop/s, placing it 4th in the Top 500 behind [[El Capitan (supercomputer)|El Capitan]], [[Frontier (supercomputer)|Frontier]], and [[Aurora (supercomputer)|Aurora]] at the [[United States Department of Energy |US Department of Energy]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20250905-merz-inaugurates-supercomputer-says-europe-can-catch-up-in-ai-race (AFP via France 24)] [https://top500.org/lists/top500/2025/06/ (Top 500)]
